Perea ends at an east–west line 1 km south of Machaerus, which stays in Perea: Josephus (War 3.3.3) gives Perea's length as "from Machaerus to Pella". The land south of the line, Herod's outline and the AD 69 Judaea face's Dead Sea shore, is Moab's and goes to arabia. Approximate: a straight line through a named anchor.

AD14 face f0046 (Armenia Minor / Cappadocia / Pontus Galaticus / Pontus Polemoniacus).

AWMC draws no first-century line between Galatia and Cappadocia; this edge is AWMC's AD 14 extent, from Cappadocia's years as a client kingdom (rule 3, an approximation). No source describes the local move: so that the cappadocia record's label point (Nevşehir), 4.9 km beyond the edge, falls inside, the edge runs in two straight segments from points 25 km either side along it to a point 3 km beyond the label point (321 km² moved; approximate). Mazaca, which Strabo (12.2.7) calls the metropolis of the Cappadocians, lies inside either way.
Added 1 piece(s) of AWMC AD 69 land (9,206 km²) that no area covered and that border only this area (ADR-0037 rule 4).

AWMC's AD 69 extent on land (its AD 69 land faces, with islands from Natural Earth land), less the 23 timeline areas and less Great Britain and its islands. Rule 3: the extent's edge is AWMC's, an approximation for the whole period.
Great Britain and its islands (81,954 km²) are left out: Rome conquered Britain from AD 43, after the timeline begins (ADR-0037).
